## Abstract

This tutorial compares the tree inferred in Tutorials 1 and 2 with four published phylogenies of Cactaceae. Comparison with published trees shows which relationships are shared and which differ.

The reference trees are those of Amaral *et al*. (2022), Thompson *et al*. (2024), Zuntini *et al*. (2024) and de Vos *et al*. (2025). The last two are based on hundreds of nuclear genes.

The trees are compared with the Robinson-Foulds distance (Robinson & Foulds, 1981) and the Different Phylogenetic Information distance (Smith, 2020), and the distances are projected into tree space by multidimensional scaling (MDS).

## Complete Pipeline Execution Workflow

### Module 13: Comparison with Published Phylogenies

#### Reference Trees

The four reference trees are those of Amaral *et al*. (2022), Thompson *et al*. (2024) and Zuntini *et al*. (2024), and the species tree that de Vos *et al*. (2025) estimated with `ASTRAL-III` from their gene trees.

The user obtains each tree from its source, saves the four in one folder under the names below, and sets the path of the folder in `~/.Renviron` as `PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES`.
The comparison also reads the checklist of Cactaceae (Korotkova *et al*. 2021) from the local path in `PHYLOCACTUS_CHECKLIST` (`phylocactus_checklist()`; Tutorial 1).

| File in the folder | Study | Where the file is | File there | md5 of the file the reference run read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reference_amaral_2022.tree` | Amaral *et al*. (2022) | Figshare, <https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.17057816> | `dataset+tree_80MD/Tree_80MD.tre` | `185926b62a0a01b3187750e664e0fcf7` |
| `reference_thompson_2024.tree` | Thompson *et al*. (2024) | GitHub, <https://github.com/jamie-thompson/cactaceae> | `Alignment, accessions and tree/treepl_cacti.tre` | `df479c182a14028aa710b508aebaa458` |
| `reference_zuntini_2024.tree` | Zuntini *et al*. (2024) | Kew Tree of Life, release 4.0, SFTP server of Kew (`sftp.kew.org`, folder `pub/treeoflife`) | `treeoflife.all_support_values.4.0.tree`, pruned to Cactaceae (below) | `319e6985225858b836ab2ff37054b3e5` |
| `reference_devos_2025_astral.tree` | de Vos *et al*. (2025) | Online Resource 4 of the article, <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00606-025-01948-z> | `QC.Species_tree_astral.tree` | `5ceb901a0555521da1a14f0815787362` |

Three files are used as their studies deposited them. The tree of Kew is pruned to its 218 terminals of Cactaceae, their labels are shortened from `Order_Family_Genus_species_<run>` to `Genus_species`, and one of the two terminals of *Trichocereus macrogonus* is dropped (`Trichocereus_macrogonus_var._pachanoi_ERR13173055`). The chunk below does this: its tree has the 217 terminals and the topology of the file of the reference run (Robinson-Foulds distance 0), without the node annotations of Kew, so its md5 differs.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# The Cactaceae of the Kew Tree of Life, release 4.0, as reference_zuntini_2024.tree was built
kew <- paste(readLines("treeoflife.all_support_values.4.0.tree", warn = FALSE), collapse = "")
kew <- ape::read.tree(text = gsub("'\\[[^]]*\\]'", "", kew))      # node annotations removed
cactaceae <- grep("_Cactaceae_", kew$tip.label, value = TRUE)
cactaceae <- setdiff(cactaceae, "Caryophyllales_Cactaceae_Trichocereus_macrogonus_var._pachanoi_ERR13173055")
zuntini <- ape::keep.tip(kew, cactaceae)
zuntini$tip.label <- sub("^[^_]+_Cactaceae_([^_]+_[^_]+)_.*$", "\\1", zuntini$tip.label)
ape::write.tree(zuntini, file.path(Sys.getenv("PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES"), "reference_zuntini_2024.tree"))
```

#### Species Tree from the Gene Trees of de Vos *et al*. (2025)

Gene trees estimated from multilocus and target-capture data often disagree.
Part of this discordance has biological causes, such as incomplete lineage sorting (Kubatko & Degnan, 2007) and hybridization.

`ASTRAL-III` (Zhang *et al*., 2018) estimates a species tree from a set of unrooted gene trees under the multispecies coalescent, by finding the species tree that shares the largest number of quartets with the gene trees.
The `ASTRAL-III` Java archive (`.jar`) must be downloaded separately.

#### Paths in `.Renviron`

Store paths to local software and data in `~/.Renviron`.
Shared scripts then contain no local paths.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Add these lines to your ~/.Renviron file (e.g., using usethis::edit_r_environ())
# PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES="/path/to/reference_trees"
# PHYLOCACTUS_CHECKLIST="/path/to/CactaceaeFullList_2026_07_01_Beatriz_Merino.xlsx"
# ASTRAL_PATH="/path/to/astral.5.7.8.jar"
# DEVOS_GENETREES_PATH="/path/to/QC.bestTreeCollapsed.trees"
# DEVOS_METADATA_PATH="/path/to/606_2025_1948_MOESM1_ESM.csv"

# Read them in R:
reference_dir <- Sys.getenv("PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES")
astral_jar <- Sys.getenv("ASTRAL_PATH")
gene_trees_file <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_GENETREES_PATH")
metadata_file <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_METADATA_PATH")
```

#### Running `ASTRAL-III`

de Vos *et al*. (2025) sequenced the Angiosperms353 loci. The reference tree used here is the `ASTRAL-III` species tree the study published (`QC.Species_tree_astral.tree`, Online Resource 4), whose terminals carry species names. It can be estimated again from their gene trees, after the tip labels are converted to species names with the sample metadata of the study.

The chunk below renames the tips of the gene trees, writes them to a file, and runs `ASTRAL-III`.
With `run_astral_locally <- FALSE`, the default, it copies the species tree saved in the folder of reference trees instead.
Output files are written to a temporary directory; change `val_dir` to keep them.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Target output paths in the validation directory
val_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "10_Validation")
dir.create(val_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
output_tree <- file.path(val_dir, "QC.Species_tree_astral.tree")
renamed_gene_trees_file <- file.path(val_dir, "QC.Species_tree_astral_rename.tree")

# Set to TRUE to run ASTRAL-III; FALSE (default) copies the precomputed tree.
run_astral_locally <- FALSE

astral_jar       <- Sys.getenv("ASTRAL_PATH")
devos_gene_trees <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_GENETREES_PATH")
devos_metadata   <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_METADATA_PATH")

java_bin <- Sys.which("java")
if (!nzchar(java_bin) && file.exists("/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin/java")) {
  java_bin <- "/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin/java"
}

if (run_astral_locally && nzchar(astral_jar) && file.exists(astral_jar) && 
    nzchar(devos_gene_trees) && file.exists(devos_gene_trees) && 
    nzchar(devos_metadata) && file.exists(devos_metadata) && 
    nzchar(java_bin)) {
  
  meta <- read.csv(devos_metadata, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  meta$species_name <- gsub(" ", "_", meta$`Scientific name`)
  meta$Sample_from_tree <- stringr::str_extract(meta$`Name in tree`, "P[0-9]+")
  
  map_sample <- setNames(meta$species_name, meta$Sample_from_tree)
  map_srr    <- setNames(meta$species_name, meta$`ENA run acc.`)
  
  gene_trees <- ape::read.tree(devos_gene_trees)
  
  rename_tips <- function(tree) {
    tips <- tree$tip.label
    paftol_to_sample <- function(x) {
      num <- stringr::str_extract(x, "[0-9]+")
      paste0("P", stringr::str_sub(num, -5))
    }
    sample_ids <- ifelse(stringr::str_detect(tips, "PAFTOL"), paftol_to_sample(tips), NA)
    species_vec <- ifelse(stringr::str_detect(tips, "PAFTOL"), map_sample[sample_ids], map_srr[tips])
    species_vec[is.na(species_vec)] <- tips[is.na(species_vec)]
    tree$tip.label <- species_vec
    return(tree)
  }
  
  gene_trees <- lapply(gene_trees, rename_tips)
  class(gene_trees) <- "multiPhylo"
  ape::write.tree(gene_trees, file = renamed_gene_trees_file)
  
  cmd <- paste(shQuote(java_bin), "-jar", shQuote(astral_jar), 
               "-i", shQuote(renamed_gene_trees_file), 
               "-o", shQuote(output_tree), "2>/dev/null")
  system(cmd)
} else {
  # Copy the de Vos et al. (2025) species tree saved in the folder of reference trees
  ref_devos <- file.path(Sys.getenv("PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES"), "reference_devos_2025_astral.tree")
  file.copy(ref_devos, output_tree, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

### Topological Comparison

The focal tree is the chronogram from Module 10, whose topology is that of the maximum-likelihood tree (all 1205 bipartitions shared).
`validate_phylogenies()` restricts every tree to Cactaceae and to the names accepted in the checklist, then computes pairwise distances on four taxon sets:

- **A1:** species shared by all trees
- **A2:** species shared by the focal tree and the trees of Thompson *et al*. (2024) and Amaral *et al*. (2022)
- **A3:** all species in the genera shared by all trees
- **A4:** one species per genus shared by all trees

The normalized Robinson-Foulds distance (RF) is computed for each pair of trees. RF is the proportion of bipartitions that are not shared by the two trees and is computed on unrooted trees.
The distance matrix is projected onto two dimensions by classical MDS; trees that lie close together have similar topologies.

**Rooting.** `validate_phylogenies()` roots every tree on *Leuenbergeria*.
The Module 10 chronogram is rooted on Talinaceae, but the family filter removes all terminals outside Cactaceae, and *Leuenbergeria* is sister to the rest of the family in the focal tree.
The genus can be changed with `rooting_genus`; trees without it are left unrooted and flagged in `SUPP_rooting_summary`.

**The constraint.** The focal tree was inferred under the topological constraint of Module 8 (Tutorial 2), so part of its agreement with each reference is imposed by the constraint and not found by the data. On each shared taxon set, 12 to 17 of the bipartitions the focal tree shares with a reference are imposed by the constraint: 27 to 37 % of the shared bipartitions in the small sets A1 and A4, where the deep splits weigh most, and 5 to 8 % in the large sets of Thompson *et al*. (2024) and Amaral *et al*. (2022). The table below gives, for the reference run, the published RF beside the RF without the constrained bipartitions, removed from both trees of the pair. Every distance rises, by 0.010 to 0.100. For example, the RF of A1 against Zuntini *et al*. (2024) rises from 0.254 to 0.312. The order of the references by distance does not change in A1, A2 and A3, and in A4 Zuntini *et al*. (2024) and Thompson *et al*. (2024) exchange places (0.470 and 0.467). Tutorial 2 weighs the constrained bipartitions absent from each reference by the support of the reference clades that contradict them: the two nuclear trees contradict none at the level of a tribe with support, while Amaral *et al*. (2022) contradicts two relationships at that level with support, Tephrocacteae with Opuntieae (ultrafast bootstrap 100) and core Cactoideae I with II (99), and places Rhipsalideae outside the rest of core Cactoideae at ultrafast bootstrap 87, below the 95 at which the documentation of IQ-TREE advises relying on that measure (Minh *et al*., 2013; Hoang *et al*., 2018).

| Set | Reference | Shared terminals | Imposed and in the reference | RF | RF without the constrained bipartitions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Zuntini | 66 | 14 | 0.254 | 0.312 |
| A1 | Thompson | 66 | 12 | 0.381 | 0.449 |
| A1 | Amaral | 66 | 12 | 0.429 | 0.510 |
| A1 | de Vos | 66 | 14 | 0.270 | 0.333 |
| A2 | Thompson | 620 | 14 | 0.554 | 0.564 |
| A2 | Amaral | 620 | 17 | 0.645 | 0.661 |
| A3 | Zuntini | 119 | 15 | 0.440 | 0.490 |
| A3 | Thompson | 734 | 14 | 0.628 | 0.638 |
| A3 | Amaral | 631 | 17 | 0.678 | 0.696 |
| A3 | de Vos | 88 | 15 | 0.353 | 0.420 |
| A4 | Zuntini | 78 | 15 | 0.387 | 0.470 |
| A4 | Thompson | 78 | 12 | 0.413 | 0.467 |
| A4 | Amaral | 78 | 14 | 0.493 | 0.593 |
| A4 | de Vos | 78 | 14 | 0.360 | 0.424 |

**What each reference can test.** The tree of Zuntini *et al*. (2024) is built on a constrained backbone of at most five samples per family, so its deep relationships within Cactaceae are not an independent test of the constraint (Tutorial 2). The tree of Thompson *et al*. (2024) carries no support values, and its root is set at 37.24 Ma, the upper end of the 95 % HPD interval of the Cactaceae crown in Ramírez-Barahona *et al*. (2020), so its ages are not independent of calibration scheme 2 (Tutorial 2, Module 10). It is a comparison tree only, and a distance to it says nothing on the support of a conflict.
The tree of Amaral *et al*. (2022) was inferred from GenBank sequences mined with `phylotaR`, the source of this package too, aligned with MAFFT, concatenated and analysed with IQ-TREE 2.1 under constraints on core Cactoideae and on Cacteae, with five outgroup species. The tree used here is that of their matrix with up to 80 % missing data (`Tree_80MD.tre`, 921 species after their filtering), chosen by the authors among matrices with 40, 60 and 80 % missing data. Its supports are ultrafast bootstrap values of IQ-TREE 2, which are not on the scale of the standard bootstrap. It shares its source of data with the focal tree and is not an independent test of it.

**Trees compared.** The four reference trees are read from the folder in `PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES`. The focal tree is the chronogram produced in Module 10, `8_Dating/Zuntini2024_young/dated_summary_hpd.tree`. 

The chunk below runs the comparison on the user's machine. Figure 1 and Table 1 are then drawn from the tree-space coordinates and the pairwise distances of the reference run; `plot_tree_space()` draws the figure that `validate_phylogenies()` returns.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(PhyloCactus)

# The focal tree is the chronogram of this run; the reference trees and the checklist are read from
# local paths (PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES, PHYLOCACTUS_CHECKLIST).
focal_tree <- file.path("8_Dating", "Zuntini2024_young", "dated_summary_hpd.tree")
if (!file.exists(focal_tree)) {
  focal_tree <- system.file("extdata", "phylocactus_chronogram_hpd.tree", package = "PhyloCactus")
}
reference_dir <- Sys.getenv("PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES")
tree_paths <- list(
  FocalTree   = focal_tree,
  Zuntini     = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_zuntini_2024.tree"),
  Thompson    = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_thompson_2024.tree"),
  Amaral      = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_amaral_2022.tree"),
  deVos       = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_devos_2025_astral.tree")
)

# Drop trees whose files are missing
existing_trees <- tree_paths[sapply(tree_paths, function(x) nzchar(x) && file.exists(x))]

if (length(existing_trees) > 1) {
  checklist_file   <- phylocactus_checklist()
  constraints_file <- system.file("extdata", "cactus_constraints.csv", package = "PhyloCactus")

  # validate_phylogenies() harmonizes tip names, computes RF and DPI distances,
  # and projects them into tree space.
  validation_outputs <- validate_phylogenies(
    trees_mapping_list = existing_trees,
    checklist_csv = checklist_file,
    constraints_map = constraints_file,
    min_tips = 4L,
    pruning_strategy = "common_set",
    rooting_genus = "Leuenbergeria",
    out_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "10_Validation")
  )
  validation_outputs$plot
} else {
  message("Set PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES to the folder of the reference trees to run the validation.")
}
```

```{r, fig.width=11.69, fig.height=8.27, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.cap="**Figure 1.** Tree space of the focal chronogram and the four published phylogenies: classical MDS of the normalized Robinson-Foulds (RF) distances, one panel per taxon set (A1 to A4). Trees close together have similar topologies."}
library(PhyloCactus)

# Tree-space coordinates of the reference run (SUPP_tree_space_coordinates.csv of Module 13)
tree_space <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "phylocactus_table_tree_space.csv", package = "PhyloCactus"))
plot_tree_space(tree_space, metric = "RF")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Pairwise distances of the reference run (TABLE_pairwise_tree_distances_main.csv of Module 13)
dist_table <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "phylocactus_table_tree_distances.csv", package = "PhyloCactus"))
knitr::kable(head(dist_table), caption = "Table 1. Pairwise tree distances: normalized RF and DPI for each pair of trees and taxon set (first rows).")
```

`TABLE_pairwise_tree_distances_main.csv` lists the distances for every pair of trees and every taxon set, and `FIG_tree_space_main.pdf` shows the tree-space projections.
The distances summarize overall agreement between topologies; they do not identify which clades are in conflict.

### Monophyly of the Genera

Of the 102 genera of Cactaceae with two species or more in the tree, 39 are not monophyletic in the maximum-likelihood tree of the reference run (`phylocactus_ml_tree.tree`, rooted on Talinaceae). For 27 of them the non-monophyly rests only on nodes under FBP 70: once those nodes are collapsed, the genus is compatible with the tree, so its split is a soft polytomy, a lack of signal, which the incomplete sampling of the genus and the few, little-variable loci probably explain, and not evidence against the genus. The largest are *Mammillaria* (118 species, 52 of them single-locus), *Pilosocereus* (37 species in 8 fragments, whose best-supported contradicting clade has FBP 7), *Selenicereus*, *Cochemiea* and *Parodia*.

The other 12 genera are contradicted by at least one unconstrained clade of FBP 70 or more, and in each case the clade places one or a few species of another accepted genus inside the genus, or a few of its species inside another: *Pachycereus* with *Carnegiea* (FBP 97, a clade of two terminals), *Eriosyce* with *Rimacactus* (96), *Cephalocereus* and *Lophocereus* with each other (89 and 72), *Espostoa* with *Rauhocereus* (87), *Rapicactus* and *Acharagma* with each other (87 and 85), *Homalocephala* with *Astrophytum* and *Echinocactus* (85), *Lophophora* with *Obregonia* (72), *Matucana* with *Borzicactus* (71), and *Echinopsis* and *Chamaecereus* with each other (70). In this tree each conflict rests on few terminals, and this table does not separate a question of generic delimitation from the identification of the sequenced vouchers or from the composite terminals of Tutorial 1. Without the 214 single-locus terminals, 32 genera stay non-monophyletic, 4 become monophyletic (*Homalocephala*, *Cochemiea*, *Parodia*, *Rebutia*) and 3 keep fewer than two species.

"Fragments" counts the maximal clades made only of species of the genus; "Highest FBP of a contradicting clade" is the support of the best-supported unconstrained clade that holds part of the genus and other terminals, and the next column names the other genera in it.

## Conclusion

This tutorial completes the core workflow of `PhyloCactus`: assembly of a multilocus supermatrix from GenBank, maximum-likelihood inference with bootstrap support, divergence time estimation with penalized likelihood, integration of IUCN Red List data, figures, and comparison with published phylogenies.

Stage 5 of the package, molecular identification by DNA barcoding (Module 14), builds a reference library of Cactaceae from the same `phylotaR` mining, measures how well it tells genera and species apart, and identifies a sample against it (Tutorials 5 and 6).
